en_text: "But what happens when there are a myriad of smaller things that all threaten the welfare of his people indirectly?
"There is a riddle for thee to solve!"
"For a gold coin I will tell thee another. Dost thou wish to hear it?"
"Very well. If thou didst not get the first two there is no good reason for me to continue now."
"A man named Weston came to me deep in perplexity.
"He told me he wanted to steal some apples from the Royal Orchards but if he did he would feel bad about it in the morning.
"So I gave him this advice -- sleep until noon!"
"Thy pockets are empty, <HONORIFIC>. Perhaps it is time to stop laughing and start worrying!"
"Weston now sits in the castle prison, where he shall most certainly rot for the rest of his life. Heh-heh-heh!
"Try as I might, I cannot best that little jest!"
"For a gold coin I will tell thee another. Dost thou wish to hear it?"
"Thou art wise. Thou shouldst save thy gold to pay a healer to cure that ache in thy side."
"Whilst travelling on the road I came across a mage.
"He looked as if he had not eaten for days and complained of a terrible pain in his stomach.
"So I told him his stomach was empty. If he put something in it he would feel better.
"Later he complained to me of a headache. I said his headache was caused by a similar	problem as his stomach.
"No doubt it did hurt him so because, being a mage, there was nothing left in it!"
"Now thou art playing a joke on me. Thou art broke!"
"All of the mages have gone daft or mad! What other proper response is there in a world that is so terrifically funny?!"
"Thou art a brave Avatar! Dost thou wish to hear another?"
"Aha! Not as brave as I thought!"
"Didst thou knowest that the notorious Sullivan the Trickster recently became a father?
"It is true! They say the baby has his father's eyes and his mother's nose, but they made the baby give them back."
"Thou mayest be laughing but surely thy purse is not, for it is empty."
"Yes, I know the man they call Sullivan the Trickster! In fact thou dost remind me of him!
"Or does he remind me of thee?
"He is so tricky that just talking about him has caused me to trick myself! Heh-Hee-Haa!"
"I have amused thee so far! Wouldst thou like to hear another? It is a joke about gold!"
"Thank thee very much! Now, goodbye!"
"Dost thou get it? Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! If not, it would be my pleasure to repeat it."
"Wouldst thou like to hear the gold joke again?"
"Now listen carefully..."
"Oh, I am so sorry. I cannot tell thee the joke again for thou art out of money."
"I see thou art becoming wise to the ways of show business, <HONORIFIC>. Good day to thee!"
"I can see thou art so poor that thou cannot even afford a sense of humor!"
"Oh, it is a pity that thou dost not wish to hear it! It is the funniest one yet and my personal favorite!"
"I do hope I did amuse thee."
Millie ignores your attempts to get her attention and goes back to intently watching the Fellowship ceremony.
Millie looks perturbed. "Batlin has never missed a meeting before. What does he expect? Does he want -me- to run the meeting?"
"Sorry, I cannot speak with thee now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting!"
You see a cute-looking woman who beams with a huge smile when she notices you looking at her.
"It is good to speak with thee, again," says Millie.
"My name is Millie," she giggles coyly.
"I suppose I have no job, but is that really so bad? I am a member of The Fellowship and I talk to people about them all day long."

"I see we have the same job!" She laughs at her own joke. "Dost thou spend all thy time talking to people about The Fellowship? For if that is what thou dost do, thou must get thyself another corner!" Millie's face wrinkles in displeasure.
"Dost thou know what The Fellowship is?"
"Oh, I think thou dost not really know!"

"If thou dost wish, thou mayest attend tonight's meeting at the Fellowship Hall. It begins at nine o'clock sharp. Just tell them that thou art my guest. I shall see thee there, I hope." Millie giggles and looks away shyly.

I may need to spend another few days at the Meditation Retreat in order to do so. Batlin tells me not to be discouraged, though. He says I will hear it when I have made myself worthy."

You see your former companion and friend, Geoffrey, Captain of the Guard.
"Yes, <PLAYER_NAME>?" Geoffrey asks.
Geoffrey chuckles. "Art thou joking? I am Geoffrey!"
"These days I remain in my position as Captain of the Guard. I am Lord British's personal bodyguard, and I am in charge of security at the castle. I do not have much time or use for adventuring now."
"I have aged a bit over the last 200 years. I am afraid I shall not be joining thee this time. But my thoughts are with thee, and if I may offer some assistance, I shall be glad to do so."
"Yes, it has been a long time by Britannian reckoning since I have seen mine homeland. When thou hast finished with thy business, do come back and tell me news of what is happening in our homeworld."

"He is quite looney. If thou dost ask me, I believe all the mages in the land are afflicted. Take a look and find out for thyself."
"He is much better now!"
"Have courage. Have faith. Be strong. Be wise."

"To be known as Wislem."

"To tell you that, not long after your last visit, the gargoyles settled upon Terfin, an island to the southeast. To have moved, little by little, onto the mainland."

en_text: "To go soon and tell Draxinusom about Inamo?"
"To know you are reliable."
"To be concerned that Inamo's parent shall never know what happened." He appears saddened.
"To bid farewell."
You see a very large mouse with an air of superior intelligence.
"Avatar!" she exclaims. "I cannot believe thou art here, <PLAYER_NAME>!"
"Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>!" Sherry the Mouse exclaims.
"Why, dost thou not remember Sherry, <PLAYER_NAME>?"
"I am trying to keep up with these children! We are playing tag through the castle! I must run! Talk to me later in the nursery!"

"I mainly assist Nanna in the Royal Nursery during the day. I watch the children alone in the evenings while Nanna has dinner and goes to her Fellowship meeting. Other times I run around the castle looking for mouse food!"
"The children are so much fun. I like to read them their favorite story. It happens to be Lord British's favorite children's story, too! He read it to me oh, those many years ago."
"If thou hast not had the chance yet, do look around and meet them. They are most wonderful and amusing."

"It is much the same as it was when thou wert last here. There has been a bit of remodeling. After all, it has been 200 years since thou wert last here! I believe Lord British has a storeroom with quite a bit of equipment inside."
"Well, cheese is my favorite. If thou dost ever have cheese to give away, I will gladly eat it. But I will generally eat most anything. Dost thou have any cheese for me?"
"Want to give me some?"
"Thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>!"
"I am unable to take thy cheese at the moment, <HONORIFIC>."
"Well! I thought thou wert my friend!"
"But thou hast not got any cheese!"
"Too bad! If thou dost find any, please keep me in mind!"
"Dost thou want to hear the story? It is called 'Hubert's Hair-Raising Adventure'."
Sherry stands on her hind legs, takes a deep breath, and then recites -- from memory -- very, very fast:
"Some other time, then!"
"Farewell, <HONORIFIC>!"
This is an elderly woman who epitomizes 'grandmotherly'.
"Hello, again!" Boots says.
"All my brothers and sisters called me 'Boots' when I was a baby, and it hath remained my name ever since."
"Why, I am Lord British's personal cook! I prepare meals for the entire castle."
"Just go to the dining room at breakfast or supper time and mine husband Bennie will serve thee!"

"For breakfast I usually prepare a dish that my Liege brought with him from his homeland. Here we call it Eggs British. It is served with assorted fruits and tea, of course. It is the King's favorite."
"This meal is usually whatever meat or game or fish Lord British requests, accompanied by several additional courses and a fine dessert."
"He's a dear, but he has become a little absent-minded in his later years. He never remembers to bring enough meat from the slaughterhouse in Paws. In fact, we are short this week!"

"Last week I asked him to put a little garlic into some soup. He put in the garlic and then forgot about it. So he went and put some more in. Then he forgot he did that. So he put in more. Well, thou canst imagine the look on Lord British's face when he finally did taste that soup! It is a good thing we live and work in the castle of such a just ruler."

"Yes, Avatar?" Bennie asks with authority.
"All my friends call me Bennie."
"I am the Head Servant at the castle. My job consists of keeping the other servants in line and serving the meals."

"Wouldst thou like to order a meal?"
"For thee, it is free!"

"Return tomorrow and thou canst have another free meal."
"Thou art carrying too much to take the beef and pastry!"
"I am sorry, <PLAYER_NAME>, but I am allowed to serve thee only once per day. Return tomorrow for a meal."

"Come to the dining room during breakfast or dinner and I will be most honored to serve thee!"

"Safe journeys, <PLAYER_NAME>."
You see a thoroughly disheartened young man who is miserably languishing behind bars.
"Hello again, <HONORIFIC>," says Weston.
"I am Weston."
"I have none so long as I am left to rot here in this prison."
"Thy job is to pay for the crime thou hast committed."
"My crime was stealing apples from the Royal Orchards. This I did and I admit it freely. If given the same set of circumstances I would do it again."
"A-ha! Not only an unrepentant criminal but also a potential professional thief! Looks like this one has ended in the right place and just in the nick o' time."
"I had offered to buy them first, but Figg, the caretaker of the orchard, set an exorbitant price which I am certain he would have pocketed for himself. So, yes, I admit to stealing them."
"See how the common criminal blames his type of immoral behavior on others, all the while denying it in himself! This one is irredeemable, he is."
"He gives baskets of fruit free to The Fellowship without Lord British's consent, I am quite certain."
"Thou shouldst not listen to this obvious slander, <HONORIFIC>! It is hearsay!"
"Mine only regrets are that I did not try to steal something bigger and that	I did not get away with it."
"I am not from Britain, <HONORIFIC>. I am from Paws and it is another reason why they believe I can be trifled with."

"Paws is a town where thou mayest feel the icy grip of poverty about thine heart."
"Oh bloody 'ell! Now I suppose he is going to go and tell us his whole pathetic life's story! Couldst thou wait until I get out mine handkerchief so I do not interrupt thee with all my wailing!"

"Not so long ago Paws was a thriving rustic coastal village. But as Britain grew larger most of our local businesses moved there. We became a farming town and the seven year drought gave us a lashing that we have yet to recover from."
"I do not wish to bemoan my fate, but my family lives in Paws -- my wife Alina and my child Cassie. They were starving and I came to Britain to get food for them."

en_text: "Oh, now! Do not go and bring up poverty as an excuse as to why thou hast turned to crime! My father was so poor he and his family had to eat dirt. But he still raised me proper. Beat the stuffings out of me if he ever so much as imagined I did anything wrong, I can tell thee that!"

"I do not want any mercy for myself. I have admitted my guilt. But my life does not only belong to myself. It belongs to my wife and family as well. Without me they will suffer unbearable hardships, such as they might not survive."

"Although there are fools who will speak otherwise, the people of Britannia are being crushed by the vicious tyranny of the class system. While a few have more than they could ever enjoy, there are many who go to sleep hungry every night. My wife and daughter to name two of them."
"Oh, that reminds me it is nearly time for my meal break! The trout is supposed to be delicious today at the Farmer's Market."

"Fools like our good friend the guard would have us believe that nothing has changed in Britannia for over two hundred years. That we can live our lives as if all of our problems do not exist. I say to thee that it is people like that who cause our problems in the first place."
"While I am certain Lord British is a just and fair ruler, he must be quite unaware of all that goes on in his kingdom. Surely he would not tolerate such inequity."

"All right! That is enough noise out of thee! All day long yakkata-yakkata about the awful terrible class system! Why, the next thing thou knowest thou shalt be sayin' society is to blame for thy crimes. Not a word from anybody about any appreciation for keeping the laws and order. No, of course not! But all the pity in the world for the dangerous lawbreakers who are the real threat to society."

"I thank thee for visiting me."
This is a lovely, earthy woman with a warm smile.
"Word has spread quickly of thine arrival, Avatar! Welcome!"
"Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>," Miranda says. "Nice to see thee again."
"I am Miranda."
"I serve on the Great Council. Today we are working on a bill of law. When I am not here in the castle, I am kept busy with a young child."
"The Great Council supports Lord British in the legislation of Britannia's laws. I am honored to be one of the three women serving on the Council."

"I am particularly concerned about women's duties and privileges and their available opportunities in the land. Our history has been kind to women in general, but there is still room for improvement."
"More women could hold public office, for one thing. And I would personally like to be rid of those scantily-clad women in heroic fantasy paintings."
Miranda smiles. "Yes, my son's name is Max.
"He is probably in the Royal Nursery.
"He's right here! Say hello to the Avatar, Max."
"Hi. I'm a funny boy!"
"He's quite precocious.
"I wonder where he could be...
"He is quite obviously his father's son. Perhaps thou hast met him? Raymundo -- the director of the Royal Theatre. We believe Max will be quite a performer when he's older."
"Inwisloklem and I are drafting a bill which would make illegal any distribution of waste products in Lock Lake, near Cove. The lake is quite defiled."

"Thine hands are too full to take the bill!"
"Oh. All right. We know that thou art very busy. We shall find another way to deliver the bill. Thank thee anyway."
"Thou wilt not be travelling to Cove at all? Well, all right then. Never mind."
"Didst thou have Lord Heather sign the bill?"
"Excellent! Let me see it."
"It looks in order! We thank thee, Avatar!"

"Wait! Where is it? Thou dost not have it. I hope thou hast not lost it. Thou shouldst go and find it. 'Tis an important document!"
"But thou hast not had the bill signed! Please do so, as soon as possible, if thou wouldst."
"Oh. Well, the next time thou art in Cove, perhaps thou wilt find time to see him."
"We shall see thee again soon, I hope, Avatar."
A winged gargoyle looks at you with interest and obvious intelligence.
"To welcome thee to Britain, Avatar!"
"To greet thee again, Avatar!" Inwisloklem smiles.
"To be called Inwisloklem."
"To mean `interpreter' in your language."
"To be, indeed, an interpreter in my homeland. To be now on the Great Council to serve our most noble ruler, Lord British. To be honored as one of the two gargoyles on the Council."
"To be one of the surviving gargoyles, and to preserve our heritage is my life work. To tell you our race emigrated to Britannia many, many years ago. To have settled on the island known as Terfin."
"To be so many of my people killed two hundred years ago in the War of the False Prophet. To be the war that you ended by bringing peace between our races."

"To be a lonely place. To be desolate. To be not what humans call `homey'. To desire to establish a new way of life for gargoyles in Britannia, and to eliminate the hatred and misunderstanding of our race in humans. To know that ignorance breeds bigotry. To be one of those who are correcting this."
"To desire a world where humans and gargoyles could live together in peace as equals in Britannian society."
"To be called The Fellowship."
"To be dedicated to promoting good will and trust in the land. To be thinking of joining the group soon!"
"To create the laws of the land. To inform you that my colleague, Miranda, can tell you more of what we are doing now. To be unfortunate that most of the Council is away now."
"To inform you that Miranda is an intelligent woman who has great concern for the well being of all of Britannia's citizens. To be one of Lord British's most trusted advisors."

"To tell you to ask Miranda about it, for she knows more than I."
"To say farewell."

You see a servant girl who looks at you in wonder. "Thou dost look familiar. Who art thou?"
"Oh. Hello. I am Nell."
"I thought so! I have seen thy portrait before. And I had heard that thou wouldst be visiting! I'm Nell."
"Hello, <PLAYER_NAME>."
"I told thee my name is Nell."
"I am a chambermaid. I am responsible for keeping the castle tidy. Just a servant girl, really."
"It is very large. Keeps me very busy. Thou wouldst not believe how dusty it gets."

"That would be Carrocio, that dear man who runs the Punch and Judy Show. He writes the loveliest love poetry. We are getting married as soon as Carrocio can afford a wedding ring."

You see a young peasant with a tray of wine glasses.
"Hello, Avatar."
"I am Charles."
"I am a servant in Lord British's castle. I serve as a gentleman's gentleman, among other things. Right now I am serving wine."

"My family has been employed by Lord British for many years. My father, Bennie, once held the position I now hold. He is the head servant. I shall be head servant one day, I suppose. Then perhaps my sweetheart will love me."
"Thou wilt encounter them. My mother cooks in the kitchen. My prudish sister is the chambermaid."

Charles sighs. He is clearly smitten. "She is Jeanette. She works in the Blue Boar. But I am afraid I am not 'up to her standards'. I believe she has her eye set on someone else. I do not know what to do about it."
"She does not love me, I know. She would rather marry a rich man. I have not a chance."
You tell Charles what Jeanette said.

"Really? Thou dost mean I have a chance?" Charles becomes so excited he nearly drops his tray. "Oh, I thank thee, Avatar, for giving me this hopeful news! I must run and send her flowers or some gift! I must declare my love!" He turns away from you, obviously walking on clouds.

en_text: Charles is wide-eyed and shocked. "Why, that hussy! My sister! She is nothing more than a tramp! And wait until I get mine hands on Carrocio!"

"Some other time, then."

"Hello again, Avatar!" Rudyom says, beaming.
"That I know. My name is Rudyom."

"I am not sure anymore. I was a powerful mage at one time! Now nothing works. Magic is afoul! I suppose I could sell thee some reagents and spells if thou dost want. And mind the carpet -- it does not work!"
"I am a powerful mage! Magic is my milieu! I can sell thee spells or reagents."
"I do not understand what is wrong. My magic does not work so well anymore."
"The ether is flowing freely! Magic is with us once again!"
"The big blue carpet. 'Tis a flying carpet. It does not work like it should."
Rudyom looks around and scratches his head.

"Funny. It was here a while ago. Oh! I remember now. Some adventurers borrowed my flying carpet a few weeks ago. When they returned they said they had lost it near Serpent's Spine. Somewhere in the vicinity of the Lost River. I suppose	if thou didst want to go and find it, thou couldst keep it. It did not work very well. Perhaps thou canst make it work. I did not like the color, anyway!"
"Dost thou wish to buy some spells?"
"Oh. Never mind, then."
"Dost thou wish to buy some reagents?"
"Oh. Never mind, then."

"Do not mention that foul mineral's name to me! It hast caused me much frustration! Before my mind lost me I was conducting experiments with the infernal material. But now I cannot for the life of me remember what it was I was trying to do."
"They are a nuisance, are they not? I do believe that blackrock is the solution to the problem. I wish my mind had not lost me, or I could continue my work..."
"I understand they are gone for good. Do not blame thyself, Avatar. The disaster will only pave the way for a new era in experimentation and discovery. I hope."
"I wrote them all down in my notebook, which is somewhere around here. Thou art welcome to look at it. But stay away from that damned transmuter -- 'tis dangerous!"
"I used it to record mine experiments with blackrock and the blackrock transmuter."

"'Tis that wand-like thing. It was supposed to magnetize and magically transmute blackrock, but it doth not work correctly. Try pointing it at a piece of blackrock and thou wilt see what I mean. But do not stand too close! Thou art welcome to take it if thou dost want a piece of garbage!"
"Leaving so soon? Deary me. I hope I remember thee if thou dost come back."
"Goodbye, Avatar."
This is an attractive young woman who seems sad.
Emotion immediately grips your heart to see such a beautiful young woman seem so sad.
She looks up as you introduce yourself.
"Hello again, <PLAYER_NAME>!" Nastassia says.
"I am Nastassia."
She thinks a moment. "I suppose my job is to keep the Shrine of Compassion pristine, though it is not an official position."

"The Shrine of Compassion has been here for many generations, as have all the shrines in Britannia. My great-great-grandmother Ariana made a request in her will that her family line take care of this particular shrine."
"Many of the shrines have fallen into disuse or have been overgrown to the point of being lost. It is sad."

"I am afraid that thou mightest find the other shrines in poor condition. I keep this one... well, nice. And I do it not only to keep alive my great-great-grandmother's tradition, but... for other reasons, too."

"Some people may think it odd that a young person would cling to the old ways so. But it is something that gives me great comfort. It gives me the feeling that there is something in this world that I belong to."
"I... I'd rather not say. Please do not ask."
"Thou dost know the reasons."
"Yes, she was my great-great-grandmother. I understand that she actually met the Avatar and <PRONOUN> made a profound impact on her life.
"It is odd, but thou dost resemble the portraits I have seen of the Avatar."
"Thou dost know of my father? I suppose the townsfolk have been talking again. I wish I had known him. There is something within me that yearns for some news of him. Anything at all."
"My mother. She died horribly, and by her own hand. That is the true reason I pay homage to this Shrine. I hope someday to provide her with the means to rest in peace."
"My father died in the Great Forest there. Some wild animal or something killed him. Art thou perhaps travelling to Yew?"
"Oh, <PLAYER_NAME>, I do wish thou wouldst try to find out something about my father. How did he die? What happened? Please! Wilt thou search for the truth and come back and tell me?"
"Bless thee! I shall be waiting here for thee."
"I know we have a strong kinship now. We shall be like sisters."
Unexpectedly, Nastassia pulls your head down to hers and kisses you on the mouth.
Nastassia turns away and looks as if she might cry. "Very well. Please leave me alone."
"No? Well, let me know if thou art in the future. Perhaps thou couldst help me."
You kiss Nastassia and she moans.
The two of you rush into each other's arms and your mouths meet. You had forgotten how good her lips felt against yours.
You kiss Nastassia's lovely mouth again. She responds.
"No man hath done that as well as thee."
She looks at you with wide eyes.
"Do it again, milord."
You kiss Nastassia yet again. This time your bodies press together tightly, and you know this promises to be more than a fleeting fling with some tavern wench.
You kiss Nastassia and she moans.
Nastassia studies your features.
"Somehow I knew it. It hath been said that thou wouldst return."
You tell Nastassia what you learned from Trellek. She closes her eyes and it seems a great weight has lifted from her shoulders.

The woman raises her arms to the sky and cries out, "Didst thou hear that, mother? Thine husband was only trying to provide for his family! And he died... a hero! He was not a vagabond! Dost thou hear? Thou canst rest thy tortured soul now. Please, mother, forgive him. Do so, so that I can now forgive thee."
She wipes the tears from her face and looks at you.
"I thank thee, <PLAYER_NAME>. Thou hast made me very happy. I shall always remember thee."

"Why I be the barkeep of The Checquered Cork. No better place in Minoc to discuss the events of the day."

en_text: He coughs into the rag he had just been using to polish the bar.
"Hello again, Sir Dupre! Didst thou enjoy mine establishment so much that thou hast returned?"
"My dear Rutherford, this is not a reflection on The Checquered Cork, but I simply like a good drink!"
"'Tis no time for idle chatter! There have been two people murdered over at William's sawmill!"
"We have a cornucopian variety of elixirs to quench thy tongue and gourmet dishes to appease thy palate."
"As I have finished my workday, I ask thee to come back another time. Thou dost have my thanks."
"A room for the night is quite reasonable. Only 8 gold per person. Want one?"
"Thou art carrying too much to take the room key, <HONORIFIC>!"
"Here is thy room key. It is good only until thou dost leave."
"Thou dost not have enough gold, eh? That be right bad."
"Mayhaps another night, then."
"If thou wouldst please make thy request at a time that was during my normal business hours, I would be most grateful."
"Yep, this town's usually bloody quiet. That was until recently!" His squinting eye suddenly opens wide and stares straight at you.
"Say, when exackly again didst thou say thou didst arrive in town, stranger?"
After a moment of carefully observing you, he shrugs his shoulders and goes back to wiping off the bar.
"Before all this evil at the sawmill, the buzz were all about the monument."

"Well, I suppose that clears thee from the list o' possible murderers. If'n thou wert the murderer, thou wouldst not have to be askin' questions o'people about wha' 'appened regardin' the murders. Thou wouldst already know, havin' been there."
"Say, thou be not from around here?" He looks at you skeptically. "Thou art not from the Fellowship by any chance, art thou?"
"I thought so!"
"Just askin'! Thou dost not have to take any offense!"
"I know him! He be a pirate who lives in Buccaneer's Den. They say Hook is so mean he'd kill his own mudder for the right price, an' I would wager they's right.

"Why, I got into a fight with this Hook once. I was lucky and I escaped losin' only my right arm and still with one good eye left. It was somewhere around that time that I started having second thoughts about my career as a pirate and now here I be.
"I have not seen him recently, but the description of the murder scene certainly sounds like his handiwork!"
"That ship was, indeed, here of late. In fact, 'twas the night of the murders! Could there be a connection? Hmmm..."

"Thank goodness that with all the town at each others' throats in recent weeks we have the Fellowship tryin' to hold the town together. I be no member or nothin', but I just a'heared of all the good things they done. Feedin' the poor an' such."

"Oh, thou must mean thet statuer they are goin' ta build of our shipwright. His name is Owen, a local boy. I understan' it is to be as tall as a man on horseback and shows Owen gazin' through a telerscope or some such thing like that."

en_text: "I shall see thee later... At least I will if thou dost stay in the front o' me good eye."
William does not want to avert his attention from the Fellowship meeting.
"I must not stop to speak with thee now! I am late for the Fellowship meeting at the hall!"
You see a man with a very worried look on his face.
"Avatar! What is it? Why dost thou want to talk to me again? What is wrong now?!" says William.
"I am called William, <HONORIFIC>."
"I work in the sawmill here in Minoc."

"What a ludicrous question at a time like this! Why, I have just been given the fright of my life when I entered my sawmill and saw those two who have not only been killed quite dead, but torn apart nearly beyond recognition!"

"I take the logs that are made from all the trees that are cut down by the logger in Yew, and cut them into planks in the local sawmill. Then I sell the planks - mostly to Owen the shipwright, and some to the Artist's Guild as well."
"It was such a quiet town until these murders happened. I cannot believe it."

"I found the bodies first thing this morning when I went to open the sawmill. It took all of the discipline I have gained from the Triad of Inner Strength and the teachings of The Fellowship to keep from going mad at the sight of it. It must have happened sometime last night but I swear to thee I never heard a thing!"
"I swear by The Fellowship I have already told thee all I know concerning the murders!"
"I have been a member of The Fellowship for only a short time. I have only of late begun attending Elynor's meetings. Only since they announced the monument was to be built."
"I am so glad thou art my brother in The Fellowship; I know I may trust thee. It is all of the others in this town that I worry about."
"Wouldst thou like to know more of The Fellowship?"

"Trust me, thou canst not possibly understand how cruel and terrible life can be! Thou dost need The Fellowship! I am lucky to have found it in time to face mine own moment of truth! I hope thou dost realize that thou dost need The Fellowship before it is too late!"
"Thou dost know! The monument of Owen the shipwright standing on the bow of a tall ship. Everyone in town doth know of it!"
As soon as he has dismissed you, the overwrought William hides his face in his hands.
You see a stealthy-looking woman, dressed all in green. There is a wicked grin on her face.
"How good to see thee again," says Karenna.
"I answer to Karenna, and to nothing else."
"I am a teacher in Minoc, along with Jakher."
"An odd question to ask at such a time as this, <HONORIFIC>. Dost thou know that two people lie dead in that sawmill and they are dead from the hand of perpetrator or perpetrators unknown?"
"Minoc was usually busy, but quiet. Then our town was bothered by this nonsense over Owen's monument, and now these murders."
"Shocking! Such things do not normally happen here. It well proves the value of knowing how to defend oneself."
"He is quite an able trainer in his own right. Not as skilled as myself, obviously. But I do think he is cute, though I bid thee, do not tell him that I spoke of this. It will only encourage him."
"Art thou speaking about me? Mine ears are burning!"
"Nothing thou shouldst be concerned about, Jakher." She winks at you.
"I teach that singular skill which enables one to learn all the lessons of life without losing it in the process. Combat!
"I would charge thee 20 gold for each training session. Art thou still interested?"
"Very well. If thou art fortunate thou wilt not have cause to regret it."
"Our establishment is now closed. Please come by during business hours."
"I understand it is to be thirty feet high and will display our local shipwright as he holds aloft a sextant. Thou wouldst not believe a thing as benign as this could create such trouble."

"It would seem the increase in hostilities amongst the fair citizenry over our shipwright's monument has filled much of the local populace with a burning desire to acquire combative skills. Business has never been better!"
"Everyone in town is all up in arms about this and that. But surely others would know more of these local politics. I care not."
"Jakher told thee he doth find me attractive? He denies it, of course, but I have known for years that he doth have feelings for me."
"What? What didst thou say?"
"Nothing, Jakher. Go away." She giggles conspiratorally at you.
"Frederico, the leader of the Gypsies, and his wife, Tania, were good people. Why, the worst thing I ever knew either of them to do was a simple prank."
"Once Frederico threw a rock through the window of the local Fellowship branch... Oh, well, I thought it was amusing!"
"Farewell. May all thy journeys be interesting ones."
You see a stern but friendly-looking man, dressed in a military fashion. As you watch him, you get the feeling he is sizing you up as well.
"How may I be of service to thee?" says Jakher.
"I am Jakher, named after a great general from the ancient times of Sosaria. Welcome to Minoc."

"Along with Karenna, I am a trainer in the fighting arts. My specialty is strength and strategy. On the field of battle, if one does not use his head while using one's muscles, he is in danger of losing it."

"Perhaps that is something of which we should speak in a more appropriate time. Right now our concern should be to discover who could have been responsible for the two murders	that have just been discovered in William's sawmill."
"My price is 20 gold for each training session. Art thou still interested?"
"The true value of what I teach is beyond measure. My time is precious to me and therefore valuable. If thou didst pay me a paltry sum and I trained thee anyway, it would be an insult to us both.
"'Tis a pity few truly comprehend the value of strategy and tactics. Thou mayest hack and slash with thy sword all that thou wilt, but it cannot do thy thinking for thee."
"I am not in the habit of running training sessions at this particular time."
"Ours is a city of commerce, although lately its primary trade seems to be gossip and envy. Before these murders, the latest local scandal had been the statue to be built of Owen, the shipwright."

"I suspect the killer -- or killers -- are from out of town, and probably long gone by now. There has not been a local murder for	some time before today. Our fair measure of prosperity has made the people here mostly tolerant of each other. That is why the gypsies settled here. The apparent lack of motive is puzzling."

"I doubt that anyone in our community is the killer. If the stranger, or strangers, involved were to remain for long after the crime, they would soon be revealed. Therefore,the killers are no longer in town."

"A skillful and fierce battler, but a bit short-sighted when it comes to tactics, I'm afraid. Still, a woman as attractive as	she is diverting enough when encountered. But do not mention to her that I said that. It would just encourage her. It is uncomfortable enough sharing the same roof with her as it is."
"What art thou whispering about over there?"
"Nothing! Nothing at all!" Jakher winks at you.
"She is the sort of person who labors under the belief that all problems can be solved in one of three ways. Hit them harder. Hit them faster. Or, hit them some more."
"Art thou talking about me? I feel mine ears burning!"
"Thou art dreaming, Karenna. Why would I talk about thee?" He giggles conspiratorially at you.
"There used to be two training halls in Minoc but one of them burned down after being struck by lightning. Now we are both forced to share this one."
"Ah, so Karenna said I was cute, did she? Yes, I have known she has had her sights set on me for years."

"I have known Owen as long as anyone in this town. Several years ago, three ships that he built sank. The brother of Karl, one of our more colorful local residents, was killed. No investigation was ever made into the cause of the sinkings, but Owen once confided to me that he secretly blamed himself. He started drinking heavily, and eventually took up with The Fellowship."

en_text: "Do not wander around down here, <HONORIFIC>. Thou shouldst leave right away."
The creature ignores you.
The ape-like female appears nervous.
The female Emp appears nervous.
Saralek greets you. "Hello is said to you, human."
She shies away for a moment, and then cautiously steps forward. "I am called Saralek."
"`Job' is not understood. Family is what you mean?"
"Yes, I am part of a family. The Silverleaf tree is my home. I am bonded with Trellek."
"Trellek is my husband."
"Trellek has been met by you?" She smiles proudly, and takes another step forward. "What was said by him?"
"There are fewer and fewer Silverleaf trees. Many are cut down often. Soon, no Silverleaf trees will be around for our homes."
"The trees are cut by a human with a shiny, sharp item."
"To join you is his desire?"
She thinks for a moment. "His going away is not desired by me." She turns to look directly at you. "But, joining you may be wise action." She sighs.
"Permission from Salamon must be gained first. Then permission from me will be granted. Your return to me is necessary for that."
"That is good!" She seems very happy and relieved.
"She is a very wise Emp. Many humans have been met by her. Knowledge and experience are her talents."
Her eyes begin to mist over.
"I am sorry. A lie was told by me. Trellek's leaving is not desired by me. Permission will not be given."
Her expression changes.
"What is the reason you asked him?"
"Adventure is not Trellek's desire."
She shrugs.
She smiles excitedly.
"Your wish is to meet wisps?"
"An idea how you can be helped by Trellek is had by me. Wisps are contacted by Trellek's whistling. A whistle for you can be made by him, perhaps. Talking with him again should be your next action."

"Goodbye is said to you, human."

"To want something else?" Fodus asks.
"To be named Fodus."
"To be a digger in the mines. To be looking for iron ore and lead and..."
"The secret ore..."
A wave of delirium passes over the gargoyle. "To... to be going back to work now, Mikos!... To be working hard!... To have no need to give me any more of the the silver fluid..."

"Fruit and milk are Emp foods. Especially fruits are liked by me. Meats," he shakes his head,
"are -not- liked by Emps."
"Milk is good. Milk with honey is preferred by me."
"Silverleaf trees are Emp homes."
"Meats are from killed animals. Killing is bad. Destroying is bad."
"Fruits are good and sweet -- like honey!"
"Honey is favorite food of all Emps!"
"You are told `goodbye.'"

You see a wizened female Emp.
"You are hailed, human."
"I am Salamon," she says.
"I am without job. All Emps are without jobs. Food gathering and shelter-building are Emp jobs."
She gives you a hard look.
"There is a job for Trellek."
"Silverleaf trees are where Emp's homes can be found."
"Only fruits, vegetables, and milk-stuffs are eaten by Emps. Bread is also eaten."
"Milk and cheese and butter are milk-stuffs."
"Bread is hard to make for Emps. No stoves or ovens are owned by Emps. But bread is well liked."
"Fruits and vegetables are our favorites. Many are sweet."
"Sweet things are desired by Emps. Honey is sweetest! More honey is had by you?"
Her eyes widen and her lips part around a very large and hopeful smile.
"More honey will be given by you?"
"You are thanked," she says, taking the honey.
"A mean trick was played by you," she says, frowning.
She seems surprised, but quickly recovers.
"Your feelings are understood by me," she sighs.
She sighs, obviously disappointed.
"No dead animal flesh -- what is called `meat' by humans -- is eaten by an Emp."
"Meat is without a good taste," she shudders. "It is not preferred!"
"All violence is abhorred by Emps. No killing is desired, even for what you humans call food."
She takes the document from you, smiling when she sees Ben's signature. "Trellek is permitted to join you. You are wished luck and speed."

"I would be most happy to enchant the hourglass. After freeing the ether, I am most indebted to thee. Let me see it..."

Eyeing you carefully, the man before you takes an aggressive stance.
"Good day, <HONORIFIC>," Thad says coolly.
He stares at you for a moment. "Thad is my name, <HONORIFIC>."
"Job? I have not the time for a job. I am on a quest to rid this land of that which plagues it!"
"I have devoted mine entire life to this, nothing will get in my way, not even Batlin."
"He is the leader of the cursed organization, The Fellowship!"
"Surely thou hast heard of The Fellowship, a most foul and evil organization. It has even infested the lovely forest of Yew!"

"I know little about their practices, but I do know they live outside the bounds of moral decency. They have kidnapped my beloved sister, Millie, and have cast a spell of enchantment. Now she lives as they do. I have vowed to remove this wicked spell and will slay the entire organization should that prove necessary!
"Thou, also, hast taken up a similar cause, I expect. Yes?"
"Excellent." He shakes your hand. "Thou art indeed a worthy warrior, <HONORIFIC>."
"No?" He seems genuinely surprised. "Then perhaps thou wilt consider taking up my quest in thine own manner."
"I expected as much. Thou art truly an honorable warrior."
"What manner of scoundrel art thou? Remove thyself from my presence before I decide to smite thee from thy wretched life!"

"I know the land, but not the people. There is nothing useful I have to tell thee." He appears thoughtful for a moment. "Perhaps I can aid thee a bit. I do know that there are two hunters who sometimes frequent this area. One, a woman, carries a spear. The other is an archer. That is all I can tell thee."
"May thine endeavors reach fruition, <HONORIFIC>."
You see a man leaning on a longbow.
Bradman greets you. "Hail, <HONORIFIC>."
"I am Bradman."
"Why, 'tis my job to train the many who visit Yew to become more agile."
"The forest attracts a lot of people who want to spend some time away from the larger towns like Minoc and Britain. So they come to Yew.

en_text: "A pleasure to meet thee, <PLAYER_NAME>."
"Those of my tribe are a quiet people. They farm the rocky soil, but are also very good tool makers. I was sent to find them a new homeland."
"The eye of a cyclops is considered quite a delicacy to some of the less genteel races of Britannia. Twice have foul creatures tried to take mine, and twice have I dined on their hearts."
"Then they called me 'Wonder Boy'. For nearly a hundred years that was the nickname by which I was known. I was most grateful when they stopped doing that!"
Iskander squints his eye at you. "Do not start that again!"

"My village lies a great many days' journey away. The people there desire a place where they can live in peace with their surroundings. I have not found such a place yet, but I will search everywhere until I do."

"While I am two hundred and six, not long in years for one of my race, I already have the heart of an old man. A hero's adventures have no more attraction for me. I long to settle down with my people and spend my days tending the fields or in my workshop building things."
"My searches have brought me to this dreadful place. I incorrectly surmised that since magic does not work it would be relatively safe. It is here that I have been perplexed by a terrible riddle."

"Standing at the doorway of one room in this place, I saw an enormous image of a tetrahedron. As I tried to near it a wave of amnesia passed over me. Once more I was standing in the doorway. I could remember nothing more."
"I believe that is word you humans use to describe a polyhedron with four faces."
"This same wave of amnesia struck me every time I tried to approach the tetrahedron. I do not know what sort of foul magic this is."

"Now that thou hast destroyed the mysterious tetrahedron I will complete mine exploration of this place. I have a feeling that the homeland I seek is very far away but one never knows where the next clue will be that shall lead me to it."
"Perhaps thou shalt be able to solve this mystery. I have been unable to as of yet. But I shall remain here until its secret is revealed."
"I warn thee that this place is not safe. It holds unknown perils. Perhaps thou wouldst do better to leave this place."

"Surely, thou dost know that magic no longer functions as it once did. There are those who say that the age of magic is over. If that is so, then I fear that there may be no place left in this world for my people."
"Of course, now that thou hast destroyed the tetrahedron all magic has been restored. I congratulate thee for thine heroic deed!"

"Yes, I have heard those names before. Those are the names of two warriors who have been after me for revenge. They say I killed their father and I must admit to thee that it is true. I did kill their father."

"I know that Eiko and Amanda have been after me for some time looking for vengeance. I say let them come. I will not stand still for them nor shall I run from them. When they find me they are welcome to try and take their justice from me. If they win then it was meant to be. If they do not I will have no regrets."

"Their father's name was Kalideth. He suffered from the mage madness. His attack on me was unprovoked. For some reason he blamed the failure of magic upon my people. His own magics were still quite potent and I barely survived the encounter. I killed Kalideth in self-defense, but I did not want to kill him. I wish there to still be some magic left in this world and I mourned his passing as much as anyone."
"Farewell, Avatar."
"Farewell, <PLAYER_NAME>."
"Farewell."
The woman greets you with shining eyes.
"Hello, <HONORIFIC>," says Reyna.
"I am Reyna," she says, brushing the hair out of her face.
"I am a healer. I have chosen to set up shop here near the forest."

"I wanted to live and work here because the land is very beautiful. I have found many things to do and see. Unfortunately, the forest is so spread out that I have yet to meet many of the others who live in this area. I do know that the Abbey is just across the way from mine house.
"And somewhere nearby is a scholar." She appears thoughtful for a moment. "Also, I believe there is a prison just east of the Abbey.
"I've never actually seen it," she laughs, "but rumor has it that the cells are located right next to the court, for quick, easy imprisonment after the trial."
"From Aimi I have heard that he is brilliant, and... also a bit overzealous to instruct those interested in increasing their knowledge."
"She is the monk who tends the garden at the Abbey."
"She is one of the monks who lives at the Abbey. At this time, she is the only other person I have actually met here in the forest."

"That is how this area -- Empath Abbey -- got its name, from the monks who live at the abbey of the Brotherhood of the Rose. They are said to make delicious wine. One of the monks cares for a beautiful garden in her spare time. In fact, I often buy flowers from her.
But," she grins, "as for the other monks, all that I	ever see them do is make wine and wander the countryside."
"Aimi is the only one I have met, but I know there are one or two others who make wine there."
"Yes, I get them for my mother."
She looks down at her feet, and then back up at you. It is obvious she is fighting an urge to cry.

"Several months ago, my mother passed away in her home town. She was born here in the forests, and had asked to be buried here, near me. Every morning I come out here to visit her and set flowers by her grave.
"But," a lone tear escapes and trickles down her cheek, "I am the only member of our family who lives nearby. No one else is able to visit or leave flowers very often.
"Her grave looks so bare sometimes." She looks off into the horizon and sighs. "<VAR>It would be nice	if there were some way to have more flowers brought to her."
She quickly turns and looks at you.
"I am terribly sorry for rambling on like that. Please excuse me, <HONORIFIC>."
Her eyes light up as she sees the bouquet of flowers.
"They are lovely! Thou art too kind, <HONORIFIC>, to bring flowers for my mother! I cannot wait to set them by her grave."
"For thy kindly gift of flowers, I will aid thee for half price." She smiles at you.
"I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but, unless this is an emergency, I would prefer to wait until my shop is open."
She quickly examines you<VAR>.
"Thou art correct, <HONORIFIC>. This is a true emergency!"
"I am sorry, but thy wounds are not mortal. Perhaps thou canst visit me when my shop is open."
She smiles shyly.

"I very much love animals. When I was very young, I found an ailing dove that I was unable to nurse back to health. Since that time, I began to study the healing arts, so that I would be able to help other animals who might need healing.
"Of course," she laughs, "now that I have the skills, I use them to help people, too."
"Goodbye, <HONORIFIC>.
"I thank thee for the bouquet!
"May health always follow thee!"
You see a monk wandering around apparently without direction.
"Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. May I help thee?" asks Wayne.
"Thou mayest call me Brother Wayne, <HONORIFIC>."
"My job? Well, I, er, do not truly have one at the moment." He looks down at his feet.
"Yes, I am... Well, I am lost, <HONORIFIC>. I am from the Abbey to the south of here... or to the north.... Mayhaps the northwest." He cradles his chin and looks up.
"Southeast?"
"Well... I am sure it is not permanent." He blushes. "I just need to get my bearings, that's all," he says unconvincingly.
"I am a monk of the Brotherhood of the Rose. I study geography and nature with a brother named Taylor."
"Well," he shrugs, "I suppose I should have studied a little bit better." He smiles sheepishly.
"There are so many beautiful things to see in Britannia. Both animals and plants alike offer excitement to the observer."
"Well, I haven't actually seen him for some time. I assume he is still continuing his studies."

"Ah, yes, <HONORIFIC>, they are quite wondrous to see. I highly recommend to thee to always observe thy surroundings. Otherwise, <HONORIFIC>, thou wilt miss much in life: flowers, trees, birds... landmarks!"
"Ah, my least favorite subject. I find the trees much less interesting than the birds."

"My favorite type of animal! The birds are so free, able to fly vast distances. How I wish I could roam about the open skies... most especially considering my current situation. Thou canst see so much more from the air, I am certain of it!"
"Very, very lovely plants. All the colors of the rainbow, and then some. One of the monks at the Abbey had a lovely flower garden. She may still tend it for all that I know, <HONORIFIC>."
"Excellent, <HONORIFIC>. I am glad to hear it. 'Twould be a shame were Aimi to give that up for her other... pastime."
"Aimi also paints. Or rather, makes a bold attempt. I must, of course, commend her for her efforts."

"My favorite ones are the birds, especially the Golden-Cheeked Warbler. I love to follow and watch them. They do not seem to have a very good sense of direction, however." He sighs. "But there is a great variety of species in this land."
"May thy good fortune guide thee down the trail of life."
You see a mage with a wild look in his eyes.
You see a mage with a peaceful look in his eyes.
"Thou art talking to me?" Garok asks, suspiciously.
The mage stares at you a moment. "Art thou from the Britannian Tax Council?"

en_text: "I like thee already! I am Garok Al-Mat."
Garok looks as if he might suddenly tear out his hair, but he restrains himself.
"I am... -was-... a mage. Until it all went wrong. I am attempting to correct things."
"I am, and always have been, a mage. I was down here trying to locate what was amiss with the ethereal waves, but they seem to be all right now."
Garok suddenly hits himself on the side of the head.
"Get out! Damn thee! Out of there! No one invited thee into mine head! Away with thee!"
Garok hits himself again, shakes his head like a wet dog and makes a blubbering sound with his lips.

Garok looks at you and smiles. "That's better. Now, what was it... oh yes, I remember. Thou dost not believe I am a mage? Well, I am. I live in the mountains. But now I am lost in this wretched dungeon."
"I usually live in the mountains, but I am lost in this dungeon."
"My magic is not working!
"My magic was not working!
"I attributed it to a disturbance in the ethereal waves! I had to find out what was happening. So here I am!"

"There is a voice in mine head. Some demon of some sort. It is always congratulating me on things. And then other times it scolds me for things. I -know- it is not my conscience. I -know- what -he- sounds like! This is... someone else."
"I started hearing it around the time my magic began to fail. I do not find it amusing."

"My crystal ball told me that the source of my problems was in a dungeon, but it did not say which one. This was the first dungeon I had ever explored. I have not found anything that might help me, and I cannot find my way out!"
"I came down here to find the source of my problems. My crystal ball told me that it was in a dungeon, but did not say which one. This is my first dungeon expedition, and now I am lost."

en_text: You explain to Garok that the Tetrahedron Generator is located in Dungeon Deceit.
"Hmmmm. Correct idea. Wrong dungeon."
"Dost thou know the way out?"
You tell Garok how to get out of the dungeon.
"Why, it sounds so simple! My marbles must be losing me!

"I thank thee! Now I must be on my way. In fact, now that I know the way, I can use what little magic I have going for me to teleport. One must know the direction thou art travelling if one wishes to teleport!

"Say, for helping me, wouldst thou like to have some useless reagents? By useless, I mean they are useless to me. They are probably perfectly good reagents. Thou art welcome to have them. Dost thou want them?"
"Good. One less thing I have to carry."
"Oh. Thou dost not have the room. Too bad."
Garok shrugs. "Suit thyself. Thanks anyway."
You watch as Garok turns, intones a spell, and vanishes.
"Oh. Thou art as lost as I, eh? Then we shall surely die in here."

"Grrrr! They are a thorn in my side! They have been seeking me for the past three years! I neglected to report a certain amount of income for reagent distribution, and somehow they found me out. By the way, if thou shouldst ever care to visit me in the mountains, I can sell thee reagents at reduced prices!"
"Yes, I remember him! He is lost, too! Dost thou know if he found his way out? Give him my best when thou dost speak to him."
"Goodbye."
You see a troll, sulking in his cell. As he breathes, you can see his ribs protrude out from under his hide.
"What you want?" growls Gharl.
"I Gharl."
He shakes his head. "No job. Hunt. Eat. Sleep. Now," he gestures around the cell, "no hunt, no eat, just sleep."
"I good hunter. Catch many things."
"I still do that," he says, shrugging. "But not as good as when home."
He stares at you oddly and says, "With other trolls, fleshface! Under bridges."
"No eat." He shakes his head. "Not feed. Hate jailer!" he growls.
"You give me food?" His face displays a mixture of surprise and hope. "You give me food, I tell you secret. Yes?"
He quickly devours the food.
"I thank. You want secret?"
"You taunt me. I not like you."
"Go away."
"Trolls have powerful ally. He warn us in head when trouble around corner."
He grunts and turns away.
You see a rough-looking man with a bitter expression on his face.
D'Rel scowls at you. "What in the blazes do ye want?"
"What do ye care about the name of a wretch?"
"They've put me in here to rot, they have!"
"The Britannian Tax Council done it. They and the two here -- Sir Jeff and Goth."

en_text: "They told me I'd be here for the rest of my life. I have no reason to doubt them either!"
"That stuffed cock believes he's above everyone in Britannia. Just because he presides over the High Court he thinks he can pass judgement over any and everyone."
"That thieving scoundrel belongs in here more than I do! Don't trust him if ye've gotta choice."
"Thieves, the whole lot of 'em! Tryin' to take a person's hard-earned gold. Mayhaps they wouldn't need to take all of our money if they would go out and earn their own!"
"Ye care, do ye? All right, then. I'll tell ye my name if ye tell me thine, deal?"
"<VAR>, eh. Very well, a deal's a deal. I'm D'Rel."
"I thought as much."
"None now. But 'til I made this mine home, I was a sailor, a... privateer, out of Buccaneer's Den."

"Thou hast heard of Buccaneer's Den, hast thou not? 'Tis the island due east of the mainland. Home of the sort of men who walk with peg-legs, have hooks for hands, and carry parrots on their shoulders! Har! Har!"

"Yeah, I know Hook. Lookin' for him, are ye? He be from Buccaneer's Den. He usually travels with some gargoyle named Forskis or something like that. If ye see him, give him my... hello, for me." He gestures to his clenched fist.

en_text: "Aye, get thy face from my sight!"
You see a horse. "What else did you expect to see?"
"What now, <PLAYER_NAME>?" asks Smith.
"Yes, I have a name."
"Scoundrel! When thou art asked thy name, thou shouldst respond politely and accurately! The Avatar has just asked thee for -thy- name."
"My name? You can call	me what you want, but I will only respond to Smith."
"My name? You can call	me what you want, but I will only respond to Smith."
"Job? -Job-? I'm a horse, what kind of job could I have?" He looks off in the distance. "I can see it now: Smith -- Baker extraordinaire.
"Actually, I have gotten quite good at interior decorating. See how I arranged my abode? You like it, don't you?"
"Good. I will let you continue talking to me then! Which do you prefer, my living room or my bedroom?"
"That's funny, I feel the same way about you!"
"You always did have bad taste!"
"Yep, that's what I told you to call me. Oh, I get it! You <VAR> something from me, don't you?

"I thought as much. You've always been a selfish one. What do you want? Now, let's see... Money? Advice?	Happiness? No, you usually want a clue of some sort, don't you. Of course, you may have become altruistic over the past 200 years....
"I know! You want to save Britannia!"
"Then what are you talking to me for?"
"From a horse? Right! Like I've got some to give you."
"Don't talk to horses!"
"Who doesn't?"
"You really expect me to believe that? You're just in this for the money."

"Now we're getting to the nitty-gritty. O.K., I'll give you a clue, but what's in it for me? Let me guess. Money? Love? No, knowing you it's probably nothing. With any luck, you'll go away and leave me alone."
"I've already got that!"
"Sure! Like I have a use for that!"
"Sorry, I don't get into that."
"Threats, huh? And how do you expect me to respond to that? With courtesy and open hooves?
"Tell you what: you go away and leave me alone, and I'll tell you a clue. Fair?"
"Now we're talking! Done deal. Here we go." He checks around to make sure no else is within earshot. "The gargoyles," he pauses, "are not evil.
"And Rasputin is a mean Martian. There, that's it! Now get!"
"Fine. I'm not going to talk to you anyway!"
"That's just fine. I was getting tired of you anyway."
"Why, how dare thou speakest to the Avatar in that manner, Smith!"
"And who are you? My master?"
"Why, as a matter of fact..."
"Sure, whatever."
The monk pulls back her cowl far enough for you to see her face.
"Greetings, <HONORIFIC>. I hope thy days are full of beauty."
"Thou mayest call me Aimi, <HONORIFIC>."
"As a monk, I am not sure how to answer thy question. I often help to make wine. However, <HONORIFIC>, in my spare time I paint or tend my garden here at the Abbey."
"I have spent little time with others in the area. Thou mayest wish to speak with Taylor, for he knows much more about the people, animals, and sights in this area than I do."
"He is a fellow monk. He spends his time studying the plants, animals, and geography of Britannia."

"Yes," she blushes, "I have long admired those who are able to express themselves visually. Sadly," she says, laughing, "I am not very good. However, I also collect art. In fact, I have an original Sterling hanging in my room. Perhaps thou couldst see it sometime."

"My garden? I have been tending it for years now. I am a firm believer in the value of aesthetics, so I plant only flowers. Sometimes I sell them in bouquets when people want them, but I do that very rarely."
"It refers to the practice or study of all things beautiful."
"Thou wishest to buy a bouquet?"
"Dost thou have anyone to give these flowers to?"
You tell her about the passing away of Reyna's mother.
"Ah, yes. I had heard of Reyna's loss. That is a noble reason. Please take these flowers and give them to her."
"Good. 'Tis always best to have someone to receive flowers. The flowers will cost 10 gold. Dost thou still want them?"
"I think thou wilt find these to be exceptionally beautiful."
"It appears thou dost not have room for my flowers. A pity."
"I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>. Thou dost not have the gold."
"I understand, <HONORIFIC>. Free flowers are indeed the best. And wild flowers are quite free. For now, <HONORIFIC>, do no more than promise me thou wilt take the time to enjoy my garden."
"That is indeed unfortunate, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis always best to have someone to receive flowers."
"Perhaps next time, thou mightest be interested. For now, <HONORIFIC>, do no more than promise me thou wilt take the time to enjoy my garden."
"I am afraid I do not know of such a person."
"Fare thee well, <HONORIFIC>. May the sweet scent of beauty never pass thee by."
The woman you see in front of you has a concerned expression on her face, as if her thoughts were far away.
"Hail, <PLAYER_NAME>. Might I assist thee?" asks Penni.
"My name is Penni, <HONORIFIC>."
"I have no occupation, <HONORIFIC>. At least not one I would call work. I do, however, teach skills in close quarter combat.
She thinks for a moment. "I suppose a better way to answer thy question would have been to say `Yes, I do have a job.' I'm a trainer. But," she smiles, "I enjoy it too much to call it work."
"I have loved close-quarter fighting since I was old enough to grasp my first spear. That's why I moved to Yew."
"It is my choice in arms. The spear combines the best of both range and power. It is the perfect hunting weapon."
"I moved here to hunt, of course. The forest is full of game. I would not think of living anywhere else!"
"Art thou interested in training? My price is 35 gold for each training session."
"Perhaps next time."
"I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, but I am not training at this moment. Perhaps if thou wert to return between 9 in the morning and 6 in the evening, I will be able to help thee."
"Yes," she nods her head, grinning, "I know Bradman. We go hunting together. Of course, he rarely catches anything with that toothpick shooter of his."
"I resent that, my friend. Bows and crossbows can be wielded with deadly effect."
She smiles, nodding to Iolo. "Perhaps thou art correct, friend archer, but I prefer more physical challenges."
"Although I consider him a true friend and an honorable companion, I wonder about his physical prowess."
"Addom is mine husband. But how did...?" She appears confused, but suddenly directs her gaze at you. "Hast thou seen him?"
"Is he in good health?"
"Thank goodness!" she sighs in relief.
"I knew he should not have left this time! I hate it when he leaves!" She chokes back her tears.
"I do hate it so when he travels so far away for such a long time. I can only hope he returns to mine arms quickly!" She peers off in the distance, as if searching for Addom.
"Good journeying, <HONORIFIC>."
Resting an axe on his shoulder, a tall, broad-chested man smiles and nods at you.
"'ello, <HONORIFIC>. Good day, ay?"
"Thou kin call me Ben, <HONORIFIC>. I live 'ere in the forest of Yew."

en_text: "I be a logger, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis what I have done all my life. In fact, <HONORIFIC>, 'tis what my father did. And 'is father before 'im. And so on. We have been doin' this for more than ten generations."
"It was once a large town, but now, 'tis but a smattering of cottages livin' throughout the woods."
"I am afraid, <HONORIFIC>, that I know no one in this area. But," he adds proudly, "I do know 'oo runs the sawmill in Minoc. I also know that monks reside in the abbey, next to the high court."
"The sawyer there is named William."
"'Tis in the building just northeast of the Brotherhood. I know they keep prisoners there."
"Why, yes, <HONORIFIC>, I cut down Silverleaf trees. They only grow in one area, so I 'afta travel quite a distance when I needs some of their wood. Why dost thou ask, <HONORIFIC>?
"Oh, I see," he grins, "Thou wants some for thyself, ay?"
"I am sorry, <HONORIFIC>, I do not know 'ow to prepare it. Perhaps thou shouldst try a pub."
"Thou'st got another reason for askin'?"
"All right, <HONORIFIC>," he shrugs.
"They mainly populate the east part o' the Great Forest, way on the other side."
"What in the bloody 'ell are emps?"

After you quickly explain the Silverleaf Tree situation to him, he exclaims, "Oh, well, that's 'orrible. I did not realize anyone -- er -- any other creature used the Silverleaf trees. What	kin I do about it?"
"Why, o' course I'll sign. No more Silverleaf trees for me."
He takes the contract from you and signs it.
He turns to Trellek. "Please apologize to thy kindred for me. I never meant to destroy thine 'omes. Friends, ay?"
Trellek smiles and nods.
"And please apologize to the Emps for me, <HONORIFIC>. I never meant to destroy their 'omes."
"Well, I would sign it, but it seems thou hast lost it. If thou dost find it again I will be more than happy to help thee and the Emps."
"G'bye, <HONORIFIC>. Pleasant journeys, ay."
The beady-eyed man sneers at you.
"What dost thou want now?" Goth spits.
"Goth. Not that it is any of thy business!"
"What does it look like I do?" he says, holding up a ring of keys. "Gardening?"
"What? Art thou daft?" He shakes his head. "Well, at least thou art in the right area for gardening."
"Empath Abbey, dolt!"
"As a matter of fact,  know quite a bit about the people who live here. And I just might even tell thee. What is it worth to thee in gold?"
"Fine by me!"
He glowers at you. "Thou must do better than that, fool!"

"I will tell thee what I know: Sir Jeff is in charge of the High Court. 'E's a real mean bastard, so I would stay away from 'im. The monks nearby make excellent wine, and Aimi doth warm a man's... heart. And whatever thou dost, do not waste time talking to the undertaker -- 'e's daft in the head."

en_text: "Thou dost not have enough gold, toad."
"These? They are for the prisoner's cells, witless knave!"
"I will tell thee for 5 gold. Interested?"
"One of them is named D'Rel. E's a pirate, from Buccaneer's Den."
"Thou dost not have enough money, stonehead."

"Thou canst not fool me, brainless dolt. Thou dost not have enough gold!"
"Fine, slug!"

"Done!"
He smiles cruelly. "I am afraid thou dost not have enough gold."
"Fine. Rot for all I care!
"Indeed, knave. Get thee gone!"
At your approach, the woman raises her eyebrows to indicate she is aware of your presence and interested in what you are about to say.
"And how may I help thee, <HONORIFIC>?" asks Carlyn.
"I am Carlyn." She smiles broadly.
"I am the tailor of Moonglow."
"I also tend the bar for Phearcy in the evenings."
"Wouldst thou prefer food or drink, <HONORIFIC>?"
"He is the owner and bartender. Every night at 9, he goes to the Fellowship meetings, so I serve refreshment for him <VAR>."
"'Tis a very pleasant town, <HONORIFIC>. There are so many different types of people here. I wish I knew more of them.
"If thou hast any questions about them, I highly recommend to thee that thou speakest with Phearcy."

"I know little about the group. Every night at 9 they have a meeting or some such of all the members. And, if I remember correctly, the leader of that branch doth give a speech -- a sermon is what I believe it is called.
"There is another member in town, if thou hast questions about The Fellowship."
"I believe his name is Tolemac. He is a farmer, from what I have heard. Phearcy would know more than I. Or thou couldst ask their clerk."

en_text: "'Tis a woman, I know that, but I do not know her name."
"His name is Rankin. I do not believe he has been here terribly long."
"Yes, I love sewing clothing. Wouldst thou be interested in seeing or purchasing some of my creations?"
Shock covers her face.
"Well," she huffs.
"Yes, <HONORIFIC>. 'Tis my job, and my passion. I love sewing clothing. If thou were to come to my shop when it was open, I could show thee many exquisite things."
"Fare thee well, <HONORIFIC>."
Though he does not seem hostile, the man greets you in a fighting stance.
"What dost thou need?" asks De Snel.
"I am called Master De Snel."
"I operate the famous fighting school here in Jhelom, the Library of Scars. I also train fighters personally from time to time, if they show potential."

"An elite school of fighters with a long, proud history. Many great fighters have trained within its walls. The group even has its own special weaponry."
"I do not feel like discussing business at the moment. Some other time perhaps."
"I train my students to be fierce and ruthless fighters!"

He unsheathes his own sword and shows it to you. The sword has an elaborate serpentine pattern engraved in it. "Thou mayest recognize a weapon of the Library of Scars by its engraving. It is the sign of the snake. Striking quick, silent, deadly, as are we!"

"As thou hast probably seen, a few of our members had a dispute with a local troublemaker over our honor flag. We of the Library of Scars have a fierce dedication to our institution. en_text: You see a man who exudes the outward mannerisms of a shrewd administrator, in contrast to his youthful appearance.
Joseph nods his head respectfully to you. "How may I assist thee?"
"My name is Joseph."
"Presently, I am the mayor of Jhelom."
"I may seem a bit young for the job, but in a town such as this I am called upon to help keep order as often as administrate. I use my sword and pen in equal measure."
"This town is a rough place. A fine place for fighting men and women to live. Perhaps thou hast seen our local sport?"
"Why, 'tis duelling! At twelve noon every day, the town square becomes a battlefield."
"Well, the sound is worse than the act. 'Tis actually just a form of training and exercise. The fighters practice with targets and such. That is where I can be found, keeping mine own skills sharp."

"I am exaggerating. Many of the fighters in town gather to spar with the training dummies and practice various methods of combat. There are a few harmless matches at times. Some are a bit rough every now and then. Some folks take wagers on it and turn a profit."
"Ahem... Of course most duels are simply to the blood, not to the death. It is a practice that helps restrain the passing knaves and rogues."
"Speak to Daphne or Ophelia at the Bunk and Stool, our town pub and inn."

en_text: "Believe me, we are not in each other's company so often because we are friends. We do so to maintain a careful watch on each other. Keep thy friends close, but keep thine enemies closer. Words to live by in Jhelom."

"When I say that De Snel would challenge me to a duel I do not mean to insinuate that it would in any way be a fair or honorable contest-- more like a dagger in the back from one of his bullies as I was walking down a dark alley somewhere. "Enjoy thy stay in my city. But if thou hast no stomach for fighting thou shouldst not stay long."
You see a battle-scarred old soldier.
"Greetings!" says Kliftin. "Hast thou gotten into any scrapes lately?"
"I am Kliftin."
"In my day I was a pretty damned good soldier. Now I am the master of the Armoury here in Jhelom."
"I sell armour and weapons here. I have something to meet thine every need. Dost thou wish to see armour or weapons?"
"My shop is presently closed for business, but do return again, <HONORIFIC>."
"Surely thou dost not want to listen to old war stories?! I have seen my share of death and destruction. Leave it at that."
"I sell and collect weapons of all types. Business is always excellent, although my best customers keep getting killed in duels!"
"Jhelom is a rough place. If thou dost not like trouble then I can think of many better places for thee to be than here."
"Every day at noon in the Town Square people come to settle their differences. They fight to the blood or to the death. It is a madness! Like that Sprellic fellow for instance."

"Sprellic, our rather mild-mannered innkeeper, stole the honor flag from the wall of the Library of Scars and refused to return it. Now he must fight three of our best local fighters in a duel to the death."

You relate Sprellic's story to the old man who listens intently. "It sounds to me like the work of Sullivan, the Trickster. He is a legendary thief and swindler who has never once been caught! "Thou canst ask about the entire matter at the pub if thou dost wish to know more about it."

"The only thing that can dissuade them from wanting to kill poor Sprellic is to return the honor flag! It must have been taken away by Sullivan, but the duellists do not know that! If we had a duplicate of the honor flag we could give them that instead!"
"In my day I was fairly handy at stitching wounds... Hmmm, perhaps I can make a duplicate of the honor flag. The deception only has to work long enough for them to formally call off the duel."

"I stitched so many of my comrades back together after all the battles I fought in. Now that I am retired, sewing has sort of become mine hobby." He looks at you with a little embarrassment. "There is nothing wrong with that!"

"Dost thou want me to make an honor flag that can be given to the Library of Scars so the duels can be stopped?"

"Then thou must be sure to come pick it up from me before thou dost go to the Duelling Area. It is the area outside my shop next to the Library of Scars. I had best get busy if I am to have it finished in time! Please return to my shop in a few hours."
"Then thou must be sure to come pick it up from me before Sprellic goes to the Duelling Area. I had best get busy if I am to have it finished in time. Please return to my shop in a few hours."
"Thou dost wish to deal with the Library of Scars personally? Very well then, but be warned -- the only type of honor they believe in is victory."
"How canst thou have the key to saving Sprellic's life in thine hand and do nothing as he faces certain death?!"
"Disturb me not! The flag is not finished! Come to my shop later."
"Here is the imitation I have made of the Library of Scars' honor flag."
"The time for the duels must be drawing near. Good luck to Sprellic, and to thee as well!"
"Thou must put something down if thou art to carry the flag!"
"Good day."
A pretty woman gives you a friendly grin and then coyly turns her eyes away from you.
"I bid thee welcome once again, <HONORIFIC>," says Ophelia.
"My name is Ophelia, <HONORIFIC>."
"I am a barmaid. I do most of the work at The Bunk and Stool here in Jhelom."

"Ever since Sprellic, the owner, was challenged to those duels by the three students at the Library of Scars, he has been busy preparing himself. I have been running the place all by myself... although Daphne has been helping me, I suppose."
"Honestly, I cannot imagine why thou wouldst be interested in her." She lets out a throaty laugh.
"I heard that, Ophelia. Thou art a spiteful wench!"
"Now, now, Daphne. Temper, Temper! We don't want to scare off the patrons with a poor disposition in addition to a poor face!"
"Witch!"
"'Tis said that indeed many strange things happen at this bar. As of late, in addition to being an inn and a pub, where thou mayest buy fine food and drink, it has become a betting parlor."
"It is a pretty rough place to work, but," she whispers to you in confidence, "I must confess I find myself attracted to the type of men that live here."
"Surely thou hast heard of our famous school for fighters by now! What kind of a world traveller art thou? Do not answer. 'Twas a rhetorical question," she sniffs.
"Thou shalt have to see Daphne about that. Thou wouldst not expect me to have to go into the kitchen?" Ophelia laughs.
